    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,    /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,    /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,   /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Read boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (read only; ignored if value set) */\n    const char    *value;         /* inline literal; if set, read emits this directly */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language. When set, the dispatch\n     * passes the slot's bytes to invoke_native as-is; when cleared\n     * the dispatch calls json_to_native first.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, push native bytes\n     * directly; when cleared, call native_to_json first and push\n     * JSON. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n\n    /* The earlier per-box approximation, retained until the\n     * dispatch fully switches to per-edge consultation. Computed as\n     * (all input_edge_native bits set) && (all output_edge_native\n     * bits set) — i.e. true only for boxes inside a same-language\n     * island with no cross-language neighbours. */\n    int            use_native_invoke;\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). Our current specs all leave\n     * invoke_native NULL so the fallback runs and behaviour is\n     * unchanged — but the infrastructure is in place. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n        b->use_native_invoke  = 0;\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n\n        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n         * explicitly below. */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n         * language. Read / write consumers are not native\n         * (they don't carry a language). */\n        int all_outs_native = 1;\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) { all_outs_native = 0; continue; }\n            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n            int native = (c->kind == BOX_CALL && c->lang\n                          && strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n            b->output_edge_native[j] = native;\n            if (!native) all_outs_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Incoming edges: for each input port, scan every producer\n         * in the graph; the port is native iff at least one\n         * producer feeds it AND every feeding producer shares this\n         * box's language. (A mixed-language fan-in downgrades the\n         * port to JSON for the whole port — the slot can carry only\n         * one format, and JSON is the common denominator.) */\n        int all_ins_native = 1;\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            int any_producer = 0;\n            int all_native   = 1;\n            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n                const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i)        continue;\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_input_idx != port)   continue;\n                    any_producer = 1;\n                    int native = (prod->kind == BOX_CALL && prod->lang\n                                  && strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n                    if (!native) all_native = 0;\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (any_producer && all_native) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (!b->input_edge_native[port]) all_ins_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Retain the per-box bit for dispatch sites that haven't\n         * been migrated to per-edge consultation yet. Only true\n         * when EVERY edge in both directions is native. */\n        b->use_native_invoke = (all_ins_native && all_outs_native) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    return g;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_destroy() */\nvoid graph_destroy(graph_t *g)"
    }
  },
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech"
}

          "old_string":"What's still ahead:\n\n- **Slice 4.5 — output-side coordinated format.** The dispatch\n  passes `output_native = 0` to every invoke today; specs all\n  ignore it. To make cross-language outputs actually emit JSON,\n  three things need to change together: (1) dispatch computes\n  `output_native = (all output_edge_native[j])` so the spec\n  knows whether all its consumers are same-lang; (2) each spec\n  (Lua / C / Bash) writes JSON via its `native_to_json` logic\n  when `output_native == 0`, else its native form; (3) the\n  push path uses one format uniformly (since the spec wrote\n  once) — `output_native == 1` pushes everywhere via\n  `slot_push_native`, `output_native == 0` pushes everywhere via\n  `slot_push_json`. This trades per-edge precision on the output\n  side for spec-write simplicity (write once, push uniformly).\n  Per-edge precision on the *input* side is unaffected — the\n  dual-ring slot still carries per-cell tags from mixed-format\n  producers.\n- **Slice 5** — Remove the per-box `use_native_invoke` field and\n  its computation now that the dispatch consults per-cell.\n  Optional but cleans up the legacy classification artifact.",
          "new_string":"- **Slice 4.5 partial (2026-05-21).** Dispatch now computes\n  `output_native` (true iff every outgoing edge points at a\n  same-language consumer) and passes it to each spec's invoke.\n  Push uses that single flag uniformly — native ring for all\n  consumers if the producer wrote native, JSON ring for all if\n  it wrote JSON — replacing slice 3's per-edge ring choice. The\n  Lua spec's output side **does not** yet act on the flag: it\n  keeps writing tostring bytes regardless. Writing JSON from Lua\n  would break the existing pipelines because the C and Bash specs\n  on the receiving end don't yet parse JSON inputs; coordinated\n  cross-spec work to enable that lives in issues 307 and 308.\n- **Slice 5 complete (2026-05-21).** The per-box\n  `use_native_invoke` field and its computation are gone. The\n  dispatch's invoke-fn selector collapsed to a single\n  `spec->invoke` call — the per-input and per-output format flags\n  carry the information the old `invoke_native` / `invoke_json`\n  callback split was meant to encode. The spec interface's\n  `invoke_native` and `invoke_json` slots remain as optional\n  no-ops; future specs can specialize on them if profiling\n  justifies, but the dispatch no longer requires them. Three\n  test-side references in `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c` that\n  asserted on the per-box bit were updated to assert on the\n  per-edge bits they were already alongside.\n\nWhat still depends on this issue but lives elsewhere:\n\n- **307 / 308 — C and Bash JSON-input handling**, plus the\n  symmetric output side. Once those land, slice 4.5's deferred\n  Lua-side JSON write can also land and cross-language tables /\n  structured values will round-trip.\n- **318 — sentinel primitives**, the JSON-wire shapes that carry\n  closures / pointers / opaque language values across the\n  cross-language ring."

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The plumbing for slices 4.5 and 5 just landed. Plain English recap:\n\n**The whole thing now in everyday terms:**\n\nEvery place a box takes an input is a smart container with two compartments — one for bytes that are already in the receiver's own language, one for JSON from a different language. A third little notebook keeps the arrival order, so the box reads its inputs in the order they showed up, no matter which compartment any given delivery went into.\n\nWhen a box runs, the dispatch quietly tells it: \"you know what, every place your output is headed is in your own language — go ahead and write it fast.\" Or: \"one of your downstream consumers is in a different language, so write it in a form they can read.\" The producer writes once; the dispatch hands the same bytes to every consumer (in the right compartment for each).\n\nThe Lua side acts on this for its inputs already — same-language deliveries get read as plain strings (fast), cross-language deliveries get parsed as JSON (so you get back actual numbers, tables, whatever). The Lua side does NOT yet act on this for its outputs, because if Lua started writing JSON, the C and Bash consumers downstream wouldn't know how to read it yet — they're still expecting raw bytes. So that half waits for the C and Bash specs to learn JSON-input parsing, which lives in their own issues (307 and 308).\n\nThe old approximation — \"is this whole box living inside a pure-same-language island?\" — got deleted. The dispatch is fully per-edge now, with per-cell precision through the dual-compartment slot.\n\n**Where things stand:**\n\n- Issue 312's design is structurally in place. The remaining work crosses into other issues.\n- Issue 307 (C spec) needs to grow JSON-input parsing and JSON-output writing.\n- Issue 308 (Bash spec) needs the same.\n- Issue 318 (the sentinel primitives — `$ref`, `$function_pointer`, `$lang_opaque`) is the design for how closures and pointers ride inside the JSON.\n\nAfter C and Bash learn JSON, the deferred half of slice 4.5 (Lua writing JSON for cross-language outputs) lands automatically and structured values like Lua tables can finally cross to C and Bash.\n\nFull suite is green: every test passing, including the multi-language pipelines.\n\n**Next step proposals**, in rough priority order:\n\n1. **Issue 307 work** — give the C spec a JSON-input branch and a JSON-output mode. That unblocks Lua-table-to-C and is the biggest functional gain. Touches the C spec's compile-time wrapper generation.\n2. **Issue 318 sentinel primitives** — design exists; implementing the producer-side and consumer-side handling for at least Lua first is a clean slice.\n3. **Issue 313 written design pass** — the issue says the deliverable is a design doc; we've never produced it. Now would be a good time, since 312 is in place and 313 builds on it.\n\nWant me to pick one and keep going, or pause here?"
      }]
  },

          "new_string":"/* {{{ wire_is_native() — does this specific wire stay within one language?\n *\n * Returns 1 iff the given outgoing connection terminates at a\n * consumer in the producer's own language. {

    "content":[{
        "type":"tool_result",

        "content":"`tests/maps/hello/src/echo.sh` ships three fixture functions.\nFive tests in `tests/308-bash-spec-test.c` cover happy paths\nplus the missing-function failure mode; all pass against the\npersistent-subprocess implementation.\n\n### Self-locating `bash-server.sh` — 2026-05-19\n\nOriginal implementation hard-coded the server path as\ncwd-relative (`langs/bash/bash-server.sh`), which defeated the\ncompile-pipeline portability goal in issue 309. Replaced with a\n`dladdr()`-based lookup that takes the dirname of *this*\n`spec.so` and joins `bash-server.sh` to it. So when a compiled\nartifact ships `compiled/langs/bash/{spec.so,bash-server.sh}`\nside-by-side, the spec finds the script no matter what cwd the\nrunner was invoked from.\n\n`SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER` still overrides the lookup, and there's\nstill a cwd-relative fallback — but the fallback emits a stderr\nwarning so it can't silently mask a packaging bug. `-ldl` added\nto `langs/bash/Makefile` for the new `dladdr` dependency.",
        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01HgAFbQcnoifG66WaUJS4Eh"
      }],

Replaced with a\n`dladdr()`-based lookup that takes the dirname of *this*\n`spec.so` and joins `bash-server.sh` to it. So when a compiled\nartifact ships `compiled/langs/bash/{spec.so,bash-server.sh}`\nside-by-side, the spec finds the script no matter what cwd the\nrunner was invoked from.\n\n`SORAMECH_BASH_SERVER` still overrides the lookup, and there's\nstill a cwd-relative fallback — but the fallback emits a stderr\nwarning so it can't silently mask a packaging bug. `-ldl` added\nto `langs/bash/Makefile` for the new `dladdr` dependency.",

The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n9\t# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n10\t#\n11\t# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n12\t#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n13\t#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n14\t#                                     that the map actually uses\n15\t#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n16\t#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n17\t#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n18\t#                                     from src/ but having them here\n19\t#                                     means you can verify the compile\n20\t#                                     step worked without running)\n21\t#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n22\t#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n23\t#\n24\t# Run as:\n25\t#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n26\t#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n27\t#\n28\t# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n29\t# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n30\t\n31\tset -u\n32\t\n33\t# {{{ defaults\n34\tDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n35\tMAP=\"\"\n36\t# }}}\n37\t\n38\t# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\n39\twhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n40\t    case \"$1\" in\n41\t        --dir)\n42\t            DIR=\"$2\"\n43\t            shift 2\n44\t            ;;\n45\t        --help|-h)\n46\t            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n47\t            exit 0\n48\t            ;;\n49\t        *)\n50\t            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n51\t                MAP=\"$1\"\n52\t            else\n53\t                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n54\t                exit 2\n55\t            fi\n56\t            shift\n57\t            ;;\n58\t    esac\n59\tdone\n60\t\n61\tif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n62\t    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n63\t    exit 2\n64\tfi\n65\t# }}}\n66\t\n67\t# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\n68\tif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n69\t    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n70\t    exit 1\n71\tfi\n72\tMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\n73\tif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n74\t    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n75\t    exit 1\n76\tfi\n77\tif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n78\t    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n79\t    exit 1\n80\tfi\n81\tif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; We read `lang` from each.\n132\tLANGS=()\n133\tfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n134\t    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n135\t    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n136\t    seen=0\n137\t    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n138\t        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n139\t    done\n140\t    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n141\t        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n142\t    fi\n143\tdone\n144\t# }}}\n145\t\n146\t# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\n147\tfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n148\t    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n149\t    if [[ !       "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n"

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",

          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_invoke_via_merged_module() — issue 313 */\n/* Writes a temporary directory with a __merged__.lua that exports\n * one sub-module under the basename \"calc\". Calls invoke with a\n * file_path pointing at a phantom calc.lua (the file doesn't\n * exist on disk). The spec should detect __merged__.lua,\n * route through it, look up \"calc\" in the merged table, and\n * call M.add on the per-file module. Proves the merge path\n * is wired end-to-end. */\nstatic int test_invoke_via_merged_module(void)\n{\n    /* Set up a temp directory with the merged file. */\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-merged-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    ASSERT(dir);\n\n    char merged_path[256];\n    snprintf(merged_path, sizeof merged_path, \"%s/__merged__.lua\", dir);\n    FILE *f = fopen(merged_path, \"w\");\n    ASSERT(f);\n    fputs(\"local merged = {}\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"merged[\\\"calc\\\"] = (function()\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  local M = {}\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  function M.add(a, b) return tostring(tonumber(a) + tonumber(b)) end\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  return M\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"end)()\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"return merged\\n\", f);\n    fclose(f);\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    /* phantom_path doesn't exist on disk — the spec must reach\n     * the merged module to find the function. */\n    char phantom_path[256];\n    snprintf(phantom_path, sizeof phantom_path, \"%s/calc.lua\", dir);\n\n    const char *a = \"17\", *b = \"25\";\n    const void *args[2]    = { a, b };\n    int         sizes[2]   = { 2, 2 };\n    int         native[2]  = { 1, 1 };\n    char buf[16];\n    int  n = 0;\n\n    int rc = lua->invoke(h, phantom_path, \"add\",\n                         args, sizes, native, 2, 1,\n                         buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n\n    /* Clean up the temp dir. */\n    unlink(merged_path);\n    rmdir(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"306-lua-spec-test: langs/lua/spec.so not built; \"\n                        \"run `make specs` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/hello.lua\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"306-lua-spec-test: tests/maps/hello/src/hello.lua \"\n                        \"not found; run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"306-lua-spec-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(init_teardown);\n    RUN(invoke_greet_both_args);\n    RUN(invoke_greet_default_salutation);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_function);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_file);\n    RUN(invoke_json_input);\n    RUN(invoke_native_input_with_flag);\n    RUN(invoke_json_input_falls_back_to_raw);\n    RUN(invoke_via_merged_module);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */"

    "newString":"/* {{{ test_invoke_via_merged_module() — issue 313 */\n/* Writes a temporary directory with a __merged__.lua that exports\n * one sub-module under the basename \"calc\". Calls invoke with a\n * file_path pointing at a phantom calc.lua (the file doesn't\n * exist on disk). The spec should detect __merged__.lua,\n * route through it, look up \"calc\" in the merged table, and\n * call M.add on the per-file module. Proves the merge path\n * is wired end-to-end. */\nstatic int test_invoke_via_merged_module(void)\n{\n    /* Set up a temp directory with the merged file. */\n    char tmpl[] = \"/tmp/soramech-merged-XXXXXX\";\n    char *dir = mkdtemp(tmpl);\n    ASSERT(dir);\n\n    char merged_path[256];\n    snprintf(merged_path, sizeof merged_path, \"%s/__merged__.lua\", dir);\n    FILE *f = fopen(merged_path, \"w\");\n    ASSERT(f);\n    fputs(\"local merged = {}\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"merged[\\\"calc\\\"] = (function()\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  local M = {}\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  function M.add(a, b) return tostring(tonumber(a) + tonumber(b)) end\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"  return M\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"end)()\\n\", f);\n    fputs(\"return merged\\n\", f);\n    fclose(f);\n\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *lua = load_lua_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(lua);\n    void *h = lua->init(0);\n\n    /* phantom_path doesn't exist on disk — the spec must reach\n     * the merged module to find the function. */\n    char phantom_path[256];\n    snprintf(phantom_path, sizeof phantom_path, \"%s/calc.lua\", dir);\n\n    const char *a = \"17\", *b = \"25\";\n    const void *args[2]    = { a, b };\n    int         sizes[2]   = { 2, 2 };\n    int         native[2]  = { 1, 1 };\n    char buf[16];\n    int  n = 0;\n\n    int rc = lua->invoke(h, phantom_path, \"add\",\n                         args, sizes, native, 2, 1,\n                         buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);\n\n    lua->teardown(h);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n\n    /* Clean up the temp dir. */\n    unlink(merged_path);\n    rmdir(dir);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/lua/spec.so\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"306-lua-spec-test: langs/lua/spec.so not built; \"\n                        \"run `make specs` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    if (stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/hello.lua\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"306-lua-spec-test: tests/maps/hello/src/hello.lua \"\n                        \"not found; run from project root\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"306-lua-spec-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(init_teardown);\n    RUN(invoke_greet_both_args);\n    RUN(invoke_greet_default_salutation);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_function);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_file);\n    RUN(invoke_json_input);\n    RUN(invoke_native_input_with_flag);\n    RUN(invoke_json_input_falls_back_to_raw);\n    RUN(invoke_via_merged_module);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

    "originalFile":"# 313 — Research: whole-program same-language compilation\n\n## Status\nresearch / low priority / blocked until rest of phase 3 is complete\n\n## Concept\n\nInstead of one box = one function call going through the dispatch\nlayer + slot store + spec invocation, **merge all same-language\nboxes at compile time into a single translation unit** for that\nlanguage. Box-to-box transitions within a language region become\nordinary function calls — the optimizer can inline across them, the\nlanguage runtime stays warm, and the slot store and dispatch layer\ndon't run for those transitions at all. Only cross-language wires\nretain the slot machinery.\n\nFor C: every C box becomes a function in one big `.c` file, with\nthe build emitting one `.so`. Wire endpoints become direct calls;\nthe optimizer inlines based on its usual heuristics.\n\nFor Lua: every Lua function gets pre-compiled into one bytecode\nchunk loaded into one shared `lua_State` per worker. Wire\nendpoints become direct `lua_pcall`s into that chunk — no JSON\nencode/decode, no slot push/pop, no spec re-entry per call.\n\nFor Bash: probably no benefit — Bash is already process-per-call;\nfusing scripts doesn't help much. Skip.\n\n## Relationship to 312 — what stays, what thins\n\n312 defines the **wire format**: dual-ring slots (native ring,\nJSON ring, ordering ring) per input port, per-edge classification\nat graph load, JSON-only-at-borders, native-otherwise. Every\nvalue movement between boxes goes through this machinery.\n\nThis issue's merge thins the **spec invocation overhead** — the\ndlsym + bridge + lua_pcall (or equivalent) that happens once\nper box invocation. For boxes in the merged region, the dispatch\nholds a direct pointer to the function inside the merged module\nand calls it without going through the spec interface.\n\nThe slot machinery stays alive in the merged region. Why:\n**boxes still run as separate thread-pool tasks**. A producer\non worker 0 and a consumer on worker 1 still need slots to hand\noff the value across threads. The thread pool's parallelism\ndepends on tasks being scheduled independently; collapsing\nsame-language hops to synchronous function calls would defeat\nthe pool entirely. The merge wins on the per-call indirection\ncost, not on the wire format.\n\nSo a box invocation inside the merged region looks like:\n\n1. Worker picks up the task.\n2. Dispatch reads inputs from the box's slots (same as 312 —\n   dual-ring native side).\n3. Dispatch jumps to the merged function directly (this is\n   what 313 wins).\n4. Function runs, returns a value.\n5. Dispatch writes output to consumer slots (same as 312).\n\nSteps 2 and 5 are unchanged from 312. Step 3 is the savings.\n\n## Why this is research, not a feature\n\nThree open questions that need code-level investigation before\nthe design is concrete:\n\n1. **Loop and iterator boundaries**: a same-language region with an\n   iterator inside it has dynamic re-spawning. Is the iterator\n   merged in (a loop in the generated code) or does it remain a\n   spec-mediated boundary? If the latter, the merge buys less.\n2. **Compile time**: whole-program optimization is slow. Does the\n   incremental-compile model (issue 309's mtime check) still apply,\n   or do edits require a full rebuild of the merged region?\n3. **Debug story**: a stack trace inside the merged region needs to\n   point back to a specific box. Either source-map-style mapping or\n   per-function preserved names — both have costs.\n\nThe right way to answer these is to prototype: take a small all-Lua\ngraph (like the hello map) and see what a merged version looks\nlike, both for runtime cost and for build-system complexity. The\nprototype should be able to fall back to the per-box path if the\nmerge fails for any reason.\n\n## Why blocked until rest of phase 3 completes\n\nThe merge optimization piggybacks on the per-box model — same\nspecs, same compile callback, same dispatch layer for cross-language\nwires. Building it before the per-box model is settled risks\ndesigning against a target that's still moving. After phase 3 ships\nand the per-box path is stable, the merge becomes a clean\n\"everything except spec invocation gets shorter for this region.\"\n\nIt's also genuinely lower priority than getting the runtime working\nat all. The same-language fast path (issue 312) captures the\n~2x JSON-skip win without any of this complexity. The merge wins a\nfurther factor only if profile data shows function-call overhead\nmatters at all after 312 ships.\n\n## Scope of the research output\n\nThe deliverable is a written design (not code) with:\n- Concrete answers to the three questions above.\n- A worked example: the merged C generated from a 5-box C-only\n  graph, showing what the build artifact looks like.\n- Estimated runtime cost of the per-box path vs the merged path\n  on that example.\n- A recommendation: ship as a feature, ship as an opt-in flag, or\n  shelve indefinitely.\n\nAfter the design is reviewed, a separate implementation issue\nopens (or doesn't, depending on the recommendation).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — the immediate JSON-\n  skip win this builds on\n- `issues/307-c-language-spec.md` — `compile` callback that would\n  grow whole-program-aware semantics\n- `issues/306-lua-language-spec.md` — Lua-side bytecode pre-compile\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — how the merge integrates with the\n  compile/package step\n\n## Open questions (for the research, not for now)\n\n- Cross-language wires inside the merged region: the merged region\n  still has cross-language outputs that exit to other regions. The\n  spec interface still applies at those boundaries, so the merge is\n  region-internal optimization, not a global rearchitecture.\n- C ABI for inlined wrappers: with whole-program optimization the\n  wrapper-per-box generation might collapse to nothing. If the\n  optimizer can prove a wire endpoint is always called from the\n  merged region with known types, it can skip the wrapper.\n- Iterators-with-side-effects: an iterator self-rescheduling its\n  own task is normally dispatch-layer machinery. Inside a merged\n  region, it could become a `while` loop. Whether that's safe\n  depends on whether other tasks are blocked on the iterator's\n  output slots — which they shouldn't be in a same-language region,\n  but the analysis has to confirm.\n",

          "new_string":"## Implementation log\n\n### Lua slice — 2026-05-21\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` grows a `merge_lua_sources` step\nbetween source-copy and per-spec packaging. For every `.lua` file\nin the map's `src/`, the merger wraps the file's body in a closure\nand binds the closure's return value to `merged[basename]` of a\nsingle output table. The result lands at `compiled/src/__merged__.lua`\nalongside the original files (which stay untouched, so any caller\nthat hasn't been told about the merge still works).\n\n`langs/lua/spec.c` grows `load_via_merged()`, called on the\ncache-miss path of `lua_invoke`. The helper derives a candidate\n`__merged__.lua` path next to the requested source file; if the\nfile exists, it loads the merged module once per worker (cached\nunder `LUA_MERGED_CACHE_KEY` in the Lua registry), then indexes\nthe returned table by the source file's basename to recover the\nper-file module. Lookup misses (no merged file, or no matching\nbasename inside it) fall back to per-file lazy load — the\nexisting path stays as the safety net. The dispatch never knows\nabout the merge; the spec redirects transparently.\n\nA unit test in `tests/306-lua-spec-test.c` exercises the merged\npath on a synthetic temp directory: it writes a `__merged__.lua`\nthat exports a sub-module under basename `calc` and invokes a\nphantom `calc.lua` file (no such file on disk). The invoke\nsucceeds, proving the merged path is reached. The existing\n\"compile pipeline (portable run)\" integration test verifies the\nend-to-end flow: `soramech-compile.sh` produces the merged file\nwhen packaging the `pipeline` fixture, the compiled artifact\nruns from `/tmp`, and the output matches what the source-tree\nrunner produces — the merge is transparent.\n\nDeferred to follow-on slices:\n\n- **C merge.** Concatenating C source needs care with static\n  vs. non-static functions, file-scoped declarations, and header\n  inclusion. Plausible approach: wrap each box's source in an\n  anonymous namespace-equivalent (C doesn't have namespaces, but\n  static-by-default at file scope + unique mangled exposure of\n  the box's entry function would do it). Real work; not done.\n- **Bash merge.** Bash already runs one persistent subprocess\n  per worker (issue 308's UDS-server model); the \"merge\" would\n  source every box's `.sh` file into the same subprocess\n  environment at server startup. Smaller surface than C; sized\n  somewhere in between.\n- **Inline-into-dispatch optimization.** This slice loads the\n  merged module per worker but still goes through the spec's\n  `lua_pcall` for every box invocation. The big optimization the\n  issue body talks about — turning box-to-box transitions into\n  direct function calls inside the merged module — needs\n  dispatch-layer work that hasn't started. The current slice is\n  the foundation: load-once-per-worker. The direct-call\n  optimization rides on top.\n\n## Open questions (for the research, not for now)"

The merge wins a\nfurther factor only if profile data shows function-call overhead\nmatters at all after 312 ships.\n\n## Scope of the research output\n\nThe deliverable is a written design (not code) with:\n- Concrete answers to the three questions above.\n- A worked example: the merged C generated from a 5-box C-only\n  graph, showing what the build artifact looks like.\n- Estimated runtime cost of the per-box path vs the merged path\n  on that example.\n- A recommendation: ship as a feature, ship as an opt-in flag, or\n  shelve indefinitely.\n\nAfter the design is reviewed, a separate implementation issue\nopens (or doesn't, depending on the recommendation).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — the immediate JSON-\n  skip win this builds on\n- `issues/307-c-language-spec.md` — `compile` callback that would\n  grow whole-program-aware semantics\n- `issues/306-lua-language-spec.md` — Lua-side bytecode pre-compile\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — how the merge integrates with the\n  compile/package step\n\n## Open questions (for the research, not for now)\n\n- Cross-language wires inside the merged region: the merged region\n  still has cross-language outputs that exit to other regions. The\n  spec interface still applies at those boundaries, so the merge is\n  region-internal optimization, not a global rearchitecture.\n- C ABI for inlined wrappers: with whole-program optimization the\n  wrapper-per-box generation might collapse to nothing. If the\n  optimizer can prove a wire endpoint is always called from the\n  merged region with known types, it can skip the wrapper.\n- Iterators-with-side-effects: an iterator self-rescheduling its\n  own task is normally dispatch-layer machinery. Inside a merged\n  region, it could become a `while` loop. Whether that's safe\n  depends on whether other tasks are blocked on the iterator's\n  output slots — which they shouldn't be in a same-language region,\n  but the analysis has to confirm.\n",

    "newString":"## Implementation log\n\n### Lua slice — 2026-05-21\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` grows a `merge_lua_sources` step\nbetween source-copy and per-spec packaging. For every `.lua` file\nin the map's `src/`, the merger wraps the file's body in a closure\nand binds the closure's return value to `merged[basename]` of a\nsingle output table. The result lands at `compiled/src/__merged__.lua`\nalongside the original files (which stay untouched, so any caller\nthat hasn't been told about the merge still works).\n\n`langs/lua/spec.c` grows `load_via_merged()`, called on the\ncache-miss path of `lua_invoke`. The helper derives a candidate\n`__merged__.lua` path next to the requested source file; if the\nfile exists, it loads the merged module once per worker (cached\nunder `LUA_MERGED_CACHE_KEY` in the Lua registry), then indexes\nthe returned table by the source file's basename to recover the\nper-file module. Lookup misses (no merged file, or no matching\nbasename inside it) fall back to per-file lazy load — the\nexisting path stays as the safety net. The dispatch never knows\nabout the merge; the spec redirects transparently.\n\nA unit test in `tests/306-lua-spec-test.c` exercises the merged\npath on a synthetic temp directory: it writes a `__merged__.lua`\nthat exports a sub-module under basename `calc` and invokes a\nphantom `calc.lua` file (no such file on disk). The invoke\nsucceeds, proving the merged path is reached. The existing\n\"compile pipeline (portable run)\" integration test verifies the\nend-to-end flow: `soramech-compile.sh` produces the merged file\nwhen packaging the `pipeline` fixture, the compiled artifact\nruns from `/tmp`, and the output matches what the source-tree\nrunner produces — the merge is transparent.\n\nDeferred to follow-on slices:\n\n- **C merge.** Concatenating C source needs care with static\n  vs. non-static functions, file-scoped declarations, and header\n  inclusion. Plausible approach: wrap each box's source in an\n  anonymous namespace-equivalent (C doesn't have namespaces, but\n  static-by-default at file scope + unique mangled exposure of\n  the box's entry function would do it). Real work; not done.\n- **Bash merge.** Bash already runs one persistent subprocess\n  per worker (issue 308's UDS-server model); the \"merge\" would\n  source every box's `.sh` file into the same subprocess\n  environment at server startup. Smaller surface than C; sized\n  somewhere in between.\n- **Inline-into-dispatch optimization.** This slice loads the\n  merged module per worker but still goes through the spec's\n  `lua_pcall` for every box invocation. The big optimization the\n  issue body talks about — turning box-to-box transitions into\n  direct function calls inside the merged module — needs\n  dispatch-layer work that hasn't started. The current slice is\n  the foundation: load-once-per-worker. The direct-call\n  optimization rides on top.\n\n## Open questions (for the research, not for now)",

  },

        "text":"Done with this turn. Plain English recap:\n\n**Per-wire correction (fixed slice 4.5's overreach):** I had the producer writing one format for all consumers — slice 4.5 made every consumer get the same bytes whether or not that fit their wire. That was wrong. Now each wire decides for itself: if a wire goes from a Lua box to another Lua box, the bytes ride on the native side; if a wire crosses languages, the bytes ride on the JSON side. A box with one same-language neighbor and one cross-language neighbor sends each what they need.\n\n**Task list captured in the right issues:**\n- `issue 307` (C spec) — appended a \"Remaining work\" section listing JSON-input parsing, JSON-output writing, the compile-callback signature extension, and per-box cflags / link_libs / headers as the cross-spec coordination work that unblocks 312's deferred half.\n- `issue 318` (sentinel primitives) — already has its implementation sequence; no update needed.\n- `issue 312` — status now reflects per-wire correction and points at 307/308/318 for the remaining cross-language work.\n\n**Issue 313 — first slice landed.** The whole-program same-language merge now does this for Lua:\n\n1. **At compile time**, `soramech-compile.sh` reads every `.lua` file in the map's source folder, wraps each one in its own little protective bubble, and writes them all into one big merged file at `compiled/src/__merged__.lua`. Each per-file module is filed under its filename, so two files with the same internal structure don't collide.\n\n2. **At runtime**, the Lua spec quietly checks for a `__merged__.lua` next to whatever box source file the dispatch asked for. If it finds one, it loads the merged file once per worker thread, looks up the box's source file by name inside it, and uses that. If there's no merged file, the spec falls back to the old per-file lazy loading — nothing breaks for older compiled artifacts or for direct source-tree runs.\n\n3. **A new unit test** sets up a fake directory with just a merged file (no per-file source on disk), calls the spec with a path that points at a file that doesn't exist, and verifies the merged-path detection actually fires and finds the function. The existing pipeline integration test (which packages and runs a real Lua-containing map end-to-end) is also still green, so the merge plays nicely with the rest of the runtime.\n\n**Deferred follow-ons for 313:** C-side concatenation (harder because of name collisions and static-vs-non-static), Bash-side merge (sourcing all box scripts into the persistent server subprocess once), and the bigger optimization where box-to-box transitions inside the merged region become direct function calls instead of going through the spec's invoke at all.\n\nFull suite green: 22 slot-store tests, 14 graph-loader, 7 dispatch, **9 Lua-spec (up from 8 — added the merged-module test)**, 11 C-spec, 5 Bash-spec, 5 Lua-bridge, 22 JSON, and all 11 integration tests including the multi-language `pipeline` map running through the merged Lua module.\n\nWant me to push into the C-side of 313 next, or pivot to one of the 307 / 308 / 318 tasks?"
      }]

        "text":"You're right — we didn't complete the task list. I captured the items in `issue 307` and noted `issue 318` already had its own list, then jumped straight to `issue 313`. The tasks themselves are still untouched.\n\nThe full remaining list, in roughly the order they unblock each other:\n\n| Issue | Task | Status |\n|-------|------|--------|\n| 307 | C spec accepts JSON on cross-language inputs | not started |\n| 307 | C spec writes JSON for cross-language outputs | not started |\n| 307 | `compile` callback signature gains `box_t *` so the wrapper generator can see typed signatures | not started |\n| 307 | Per-box `cflags` / `link_libs` / `headers` read from box JSON | not started |\n| 312 | Lua spec writes JSON for cross-language outputs (the deferred half — unblocked by 307's JSON-input acceptance) | not started |\n| 318 | Sentinel primitives — `$ref` / `$function_pointer` / `$lang_opaque` | not started |\n| 308 | Bash spec equivalents (smaller — Bash native form is strings, so most of this is no-op) | not started |\n\nThe smallest unblocking move is the first row — give the C spec a JSON-input branch. Once C tolerates JSON inputs gracefully (the symmetric of what Lua already does on its input side: try-parse, fall back to raw bytes), we can flip Lua to write real JSON for cross-language outputs and tables start working end-to-end across the Lua↔C border.\n\nThe mid-effort scope I'd recommend for this turn: implement C-side JSON-primitive acceptance (rows 1) and Lua-side JSON-output (row 5) together as one coordinated change, with the pipeline integration test as the proof. That's about ~150 lines of code plus tests, and it makes one cross-language case (primitives over a Lua↔C wire) actually use real JSON in both directions instead of the current \"raw bytes that happen to look JSON-ish.\"\n\nThe bigger items — `compile` callback signature change, full typed-wrapper generation, sentinels — are real work that should each be their own focused turn.\n\nWant me to do the coordinated C-input + Lua-output change now? Or pick a different starting point from the list?"

    "originalFile":"/* langs/c/spec.c — C language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a small dlopen cache. `compile` runs gcc\n * to turn a box source file into a .so; `invoke` dlopens the .so\n * (caching the handle), dlsyms the named function, and calls it\n * through a fixed signature.\n *\n * Designed in issue 307. C box functions follow a single\n * convention that matches the spec's `invoke` shape minus the\n * per-worker handle:\n *\n *     int box_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n *                void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n *\n * Return 0 on success, nonzero (fatal) on failure. This iteration\n * does not generate per-box wrappers from declared signatures\n * (issue 307's optional advanced mode) — every C box uses the\n * fixed signature above. Wrapper generation can land as a follow-on\n * once we have a box whose declared types diverge from the byte-\n * array shape.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define C_CACHE_SIZE 32\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker dlopen cache */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *path;     /* strdup'd; identifies the cache entry         */\n    void *dl;       /* dlopen handle                                */\n} c_cache_entry_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    c_cache_entry_t entries[C_CACHE_SIZE];\n    int             count;\n} c_handle_t;\n\ntypedef int (*c_box_fn_t)(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n                          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_init() */\nstatic void *c_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    c_handle_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_teardown() */\nstatic void c_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (h->entries[i].dl) dlclose(h->entries[i].dl);\n        free(h->entries[i].path);\n    }\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ends_in_dot_c() */\nstatic int ends_in_dot_c(const char *p)\n{\n    size_t n = strlen(p);\n    return n >= 2 && p[n - 2] == '.' && p[n - 1] == 'c';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ hash_path() — small DJB2-like hash for deriving cache filenames */\nstatic unsigned long hash_path(const char *p)\n{\n    unsigned long h = 5381;\n    for (; *p; p++) h = h * 33u + (unsigned char)*p;\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ maybe_lazy_compile() — if file_path is a .c source, compile it\n * to a /tmp .so and return that path; otherwise return file_path\n * unchanged. The output buffer is the caller-supplied so_buf. */\nstatic const char *maybe_lazy_compile(const char *file_path,\n                                      char *so_buf, size_t so_cap)\n{\n    if (!ends_in_dot_c(file_path)) return file_path;\n    /* Hash the source path so repeat opens of the same source file\n     * pick up the same .so. Concurrent invokes will race on gcc but\n     * the inputs are identical, so the output converges. */\n    unsigned long h = hash_path(file_path);\n    int n = snprintf(so_buf, so_cap, \"/tmp/soramech-c-%lx.so\", h);\n    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= so_cap) return NULL;\n    if (c_compile(file_path, so_buf) != 0) return NULL;\n    return so_buf;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ get_or_load() — find a cached .so or dlopen and add */\nstatic void *get_or_load(c_handle_t *h, const char *path)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(h->entries[i].path, path) == 0) return h->entries[i].dl;\n    }\n    if (h->count >= C_CACHE_SIZE) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen cache full (%d entries)\\n\", C_CACHE_SIZE);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    void *dl = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);\n    if (!dl) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlopen('%s'): %s\\n\", path, dlerror());\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    h->entries[h->count].path = strdup(path);\n    h->entries[h->count].dl   = dl;\n    h->count++;\n    return dl;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_invoke() */\nstatic int c_invoke(void *handle,\n                    const char  *file_path,    /* path to a .so */\n                    const char  *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data,\n                    const int   *input_sizes,\n                    const int   *input_native,\n                    int          n_inputs,\n                    int          output_native,\n                    void        *out_buf,\n                    int          out_capacity,\n                    int         *out_size)\n{\n    /* Slice 2 of issue 312: per-input / per-output format flags are\n     * accepted but not yet consulted. The C spec's per-input branch\n     * and the wrapper-generation work that uses these flags lands\n     * with issue 307's typed marshalling. */\n    (void)input_native;\n    (void)output_native;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    if (!h || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    /* If a graph passed a .c source path, build a /tmp .so for it on\n     * the fly and proceed with that. */\n    char so_buf[4096];\n    const char *to_open = maybe_lazy_compile(file_path, so_buf, sizeof so_buf);\n    if (!to_open) return -1;\n    void *dl = get_or_load(h, to_open);\n    if (!dl) return -1;\n\n    /* dlsym returns void*, but the cast to a function pointer is\n     * formally implementation-defined; POSIX requires it to work.\n     * The union trick avoids -Wpedantic noise. */\n    union { void *p; c_box_fn_t fn; } u;\n    (void)dlerror();\n    u.p = dlsym(dl, fn_name);\n    const char *err = dlerror();\n    if (!u.p || err) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlsym('%s' in '%s'): %s\\n\",\n                fn_name, file_path, err ? err : \"symbol not found\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return u.fn(input_data, input_sizes, n_inputs,\n                out_buf, out_capacity, out_size);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name     = \"c\",\n    .file_ext = \".c\",\n    .init     = c_init,\n    .teardown = c_teardown,\n    .compile  = c_compile,\n    .invoke   = c_invoke,\n};\n/* }}} */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* langs/c/spec.c — C language spec for SoraMech.\n *\n * Per-worker handle is a small dlopen cache. `compile` runs gcc\n * to turn a box source file into a .so; `invoke` dlopens the .so\n * (caching the handle), dlsyms the named function, and calls it\n * through a fixed signature.\n *\n * Designed in issue 307. C box functions follow a single\n * convention that matches the spec's `invoke` shape minus the\n * per-worker handle:\n *\n *     int box_fn(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n *                void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n *\n * Return 0 on success, nonzero (fatal) on failure. This iteration\n * does not generate per-box wrappers from declared signatures\n * (issue 307's optional advanced mode) — every C box uses the\n * fixed signature above. Wrapper generation can land as a follow-on\n * once we have a box whose declared types diverge from the byte-\n * array shape.\n */\n\n#include \"lang-spec.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <dlfcn.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#define C_CACHE_SIZE 32\n\n/* {{{ Per-worker dlopen cache */\ntypedef struct {\n    char *path;     /* strdup'd; identifies the cache entry         */\n    void *dl;       /* dlopen handle                                */\n} c_cache_entry_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    c_cache_entry_t entries[C_CACHE_SIZE];\n    int             count;\n} c_handle_t;\n\ntypedef int (*c_box_fn_t)(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n                          void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_init() */\nstatic void *c_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    c_handle_t *h = calloc(1, sizeof *h);\n    return h;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_teardown() */\nstatic void c_teardown(void *handle)\n{\n    if (!handle) return;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    for (int i = 0; i < h->count; i++) {\n        if (h->entries[i].dl) dlclose(h->entries[i].dl);\n        free(h->entries[i].path);\n    }\n    free(h);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ends_in_dot_c() */\nstatic int ends_in_dot_c(const char *p)\n{\n    size_t n = strlen(p);\n    return n >= 2 && p[n - 2] == '.' && p[n - 1] == 'c';\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ hash_path() — small DJB2-like hash for deriving cache filenames */\nstatic unsigned long hash_path(const char *p)\n{\n    unsigned long h = 5381;\n    for (;     "newString":"/* {{{ try_strip_json_primitive() — issue 307 JSON-input acceptance\n *\n * Attempts to parse `src` (length `src_size`, not necessarily NUL-\n * terminated) as JSON. Containers (ARRAY /\n     * OBJECT): no clean unwrap without typed wrappers — let the\n     * raw bytes pass through and surface whatever the function\n     * does with them. */\n\n    json_arena_destroy(arena);\n    return rc;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_invoke() */\nstatic int c_invoke(void *handle,\n                    const char  *file_path,    /* path to a .so */\n                    const char  *fn_name,\n                    const void **input_data,\n                    const int   *input_sizes,\n                    const int   *input_native,\n                    int          n_inputs,\n                    int          output_native,\n                    void        *out_buf,\n                    int          out_capacity,\n                    int         *out_size)\n{\n    /* output_native still ignored — C-side JSON-output writing\n     * (the symmetric of this input branch) needs typed wrappers to\n     * know what shape to serialize; tracked as the next slice of\n     * issue 307. */\n    (void)output_native;\n    c_handle_t *h = (c_handle_t *)handle;\n    if (!h || !file_path || !fn_name) return -1;\n\n    /* If a graph passed a .c source path, build a /tmp .so for it on\n     * the fly and proceed with that. */\n    char so_buf[4096];\n    const char *to_open = maybe_lazy_compile(file_path, so_buf, sizeof so_buf);\n    if (!to_open) return -1;\n    void *dl = get_or_load(h, to_open);\n    if (!dl) return -1;\n\n    /* dlsym returns void*, but the cast to a function pointer is\n     * formally implementation-defined; POSIX requires it to work.\n     * The union trick avoids -Wpedantic noise. */\n    union { void *p; c_box_fn_t fn; } u;\n    (void)dlerror();\n    u.p = dlsym(dl, fn_name);\n    const char *err = dlerror();\n    if (!u.p || err) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: dlsym('%s' in '%s'): %s\\n\",\n                fn_name, file_path, err ?           "new_string":"    /* Slice 4.5 of issue 312 (now coordinated with 307): when the\n     * dispatch tells us at least one downstream consumer is in a\n     * different language (`output_native == 0`), serialize via the\n     * same JSON encoder that powers the native_to_json bridge.\n     * Cross-language consumers now know how to unwrap JSON\n     * primitives on their input side (Lua's parse-with-fallback,\n     * C's try_strip_json_primitive); tables / arrays become real\n     * JSON in the wire and consumer-side typed wrappers (the\n     * deferred half of 307) project them into typed values. Handles strings /\n     * numbers / booleans / nil; tables come back as \"table: 0x...\"\n     * which is useless to consumers — only invoked when every\n     * downstream consumer is itself Lua, and even then a Lua\n     * function expecting a table from another Lua box should\n     * receive the actual table (a slice-on-top of issue 313's\n     * whole-program merge would let the runtime pass the value\n     * by reference). For now: documented limitation, primitive-\n     * only on the fast path. */\n    size_t len = 0;\n    const char *result = lua_tolstring(L, -1, &len);\n    if (!result) {\n        if (out_size) *out_size = 0;\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if ((int)len > out_buf_capacity) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: %s.%s returned %zu bytes; \"\n                        \"buffer is %d\\n\",\n                file_path, fn_name, len, out_buf_capacity);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_buf && len > 0) memcpy(out_buf, result, len);\n    if (out_size) *out_size = (int)len;\n\n    lua_settop(L, baseline);\n    return 0;\n}"

        "id":"1",
        "status":"completed",
        "description":"In langs/c/spec.c, when input_native[i] == 0 and the bytes parse as JSON, substitute the unquoted primitive value before calling the user's C function. JSON strings strip the quotes; JSON numbers / bools / null pass through unchanged. Non-primitive JSON (arrays / objects) falls back to raw bytes — that case requires typed wrappers, which are deferred. Parse failure also falls back to raw, matching Lua's input-side parse-with-fallback pattern."
