        "input":{
          "replace_all":false,
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/307-c-spec-test.c",
          "old_string":"/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/c/spec.so\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/echo.c\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"307-c-spec-test: spec or fixture not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"307-c-spec-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(compile_succeeds);\n    RUN(invoke_echo);\n    RUN(invoke_concat);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_symbol);\n    RUN(compile_bad_source_fails);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_invoke_json_string_input() — issue 307 JSON-input acceptance */\n/* When input_native[i] = 0 and the bytes are a JSON string, the C\n * spec strips the quotes so the user's function sees the inner\n * text. echo(s) returns whatever it received; if the strip works\n * the function gets \"hello\" without quotes, not \"\\\"hello\\\"\". */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_string_input(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    /* A JSON string `\"hello\"` — 7 bytes including the quotes. */\n    const char *json_str = \"\\\"hello\\\"\";\n    const void *args[1]    = { json_str };\n    int         sizes[1]   = { (int)strlen(json_str) };\n    int         native[1]  = { 0 };   /* JSON */\n    char buf[64];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 5);                   /* \"hello\" minus the quotes */\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hello\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_json_number_input() — passthrough on primitive */\n/* JSON numbers stay as raw bytes — \"42\" is already the form C's\n * atoi / strtol expect. The C function receives the bytes unchanged. */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_number_input(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    const char *json_num   = \"42\";\n    const void *args[1]    = { json_num };\n    int         sizes[1]   = { 2 };\n    int         native[1]  = { 0 };   /* JSON */\n    char buf[16];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 2);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json() — robustness */\n/* When the bytes don't parse as JSON, the C spec passes them\n * through unchanged. Lets cross-language producers that don't yet\n * emit real JSON (other languages, future specs) keep working. */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    /* Raw \"hello\" with no quotes — not valid JSON; should pass\n     * through unchanged. */\n    const char *raw       = \"hello\";\n    const void *args[1]   = { raw };\n    int         sizes[1]  = { 5 };\n    int         native[1] = { 0 };   /* JSON-flag but not actually JSON */\n    char buf[16];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 5);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hello\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/c/spec.so\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/echo.c\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"307-c-spec-test: spec or fixture not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"307-c-spec-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(compile_succeeds);\n    RUN(invoke_echo);\n    RUN(invoke_concat);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_symbol);\n    RUN(compile_bad_source_fails);\n    RUN(invoke_json_string_input);\n    RUN(invoke_json_number_input);\n    RUN(invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */"

    "newString":"/* {{{ test_invoke_json_string_input() — issue 307 JSON-input acceptance */\n/* When input_native[i] = 0 and the bytes are a JSON string, the C\n * spec strips the quotes so the user's function sees the inner\n * text. echo(s) returns whatever it received; if the strip works\n * the function gets \"hello\" without quotes, not \"\\\"hello\\\"\". */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_string_input(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    /* A JSON string `\"hello\"` — 7 bytes including the quotes. */\n    const char *json_str = \"\\\"hello\\\"\";\n    const void *args[1]    = { json_str };\n    int         sizes[1]   = { (int)strlen(json_str) };\n    int         native[1]  = { 0 };   /* JSON */\n    char buf[64];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 5);                   /* \"hello\" minus the quotes */\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hello\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_json_number_input() — passthrough on primitive */\n/* JSON numbers stay as raw bytes — \"42\" is already the form C's\n * atoi / strtol expect. The C function receives the bytes unchanged. */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_number_input(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    const char *json_num   = \"42\";\n    const void *args[1]    = { json_num };\n    int         sizes[1]   = { 2 };\n    int         native[1]  = { 0 };   /* JSON */\n    char buf[16];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 2);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json() — robustness */\n/* When the bytes don't parse as JSON, the C spec passes them\n * through unchanged. Lets cross-language producers that don't yet\n * emit real JSON (other languages, future specs) keep working. */\nstatic int test_invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    /* Raw \"hello\" with no quotes — not valid JSON; should pass\n     * through unchanged. */\n    const char *raw       = \"hello\";\n    const void *args[1]   = { raw };\n    int         sizes[1]  = { 5 };\n    int         native[1] = { 0 };   /* JSON-flag but not actually JSON */\n    char buf[16];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, native, 1, 0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 5);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hello\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/c/spec.so\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/echo.c\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"307-c-spec-test: spec or fixture not built; \"\n                        \"run from project root with `make` first\\n\");\n        return 2;\n    }\n    printf(\"307-c-spec-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(compile_succeeds);\n    RUN(invoke_echo);\n    RUN(invoke_concat);\n    RUN(invoke_missing_symbol);\n    RUN(compile_bad_source_fails);\n    RUN(invoke_json_string_input);\n    RUN(invoke_json_number_input);\n    RUN(invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\", g_pass, g_fail);\n    return g_fail == 0 ? 0 : 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

          "old_string":"## Remaining work (to unblock issue 312's deferred output side)\n\n1. **JSON-input parsing.** When `input_native[i] == 0` on a C\n   box's invoke, the bytes are JSON from a cross-language\n   producer. The C spec needs to parse them (via the vendored\n   cJSON or equivalent) into typed values the user's function\n   can consume. The generated wrapper is the natural place —\n   per-port: if native, treat input bytes as the declared C\n   type's representation; if JSON, parse and project.\n2. **JSON-output writing.** When `output_native == 0`, the C\n   spec writes a JSON serialization of the return value rather\n   than the user function's raw bytes. The wrapper knows the\n   return type, so it can construct the JSON shape.\n3. **`compile` callback signature extension** to accept\n   `const box_t *box`. The wrapper generator needs the box's\n   input/output declarations to know what types to marshal.\n   Touches `langs/lang-spec.h` and every spec's `compile` stub.\n4. **Per-box cflags / link_libs / headers.** Surfaced by the\n   \"library function call without user-written source\" use case\n   in this issue's body. Reads from the box JSON.\n\nDone in this slice unblocks the deferred half of 312's slice 4.5\n(Lua writing JSON for cross-language outputs lands cleanly once\nC consumers know how to read it).",
          "new_string":"## Remaining work (to unblock issue 312's deferred output side)\n\n1. ~~**JSON-input parsing (primitive level).** Done 2026-05-21.~~\n   See implementation log below.\n2. **JSON-output writing.** When `output_native == 0`, the C\n   spec writes a JSON serialization of the return value rather\n   than the user function's raw bytes. The wrapper knows the\n   return type, so it can construct the JSON shape. Symmetric\n   to (1); pending typed-wrapper generation so the spec knows\n   what shape to serialize.\n3. **`compile` callback signature extension** to accept\n   `const box_t *box`. The wrapper generator needs the box's\n   input/output declarations to know what types to marshal.\n   Touches `langs/lang-spec.h` and every spec's `compile` stub.\n4. **Per-box cflags / link_libs / headers.** Surfaced by the\n   \"library function call without user-written source\" use case\n   in this issue's body. Reads from the box JSON.\n\n## Implementation log (continued)\n\n### JSON-input acceptance (primitive level) — 2026-05-21\n\n`langs/c/spec.c` gains `try_strip_json_primitive`, called per\ninput port when `input_native[i] == 0`. Behavior:\n\n- JSON string `\"hello\"` → user function receives the unquoted\n  bytes `hello` (5 bytes, no quotes).\n- JSON number / bool / null → passthrough; the JSON\n  representation is already the form the C function's\n  `atol` / `strncmp` / etc. expect.\n- JSON arrays / objects → passthrough (raw bytes); proper\n  projection needs the typed-wrapper generation that's still\n  ahead in items 2-4 above.\n- Parse failure → passthrough. Matches Lua's input-side\n  parse-with-fallback so producers that don't yet emit real\n  JSON keep working.\n\nThe C spec's `invoke` reuses a stack-allocated scratch matrix\n(`scratch[C_MAX_INPUTS][4096]`) — the substituted bytes live\ninside the invoke's frame so the lifetime question is trivial,\nand no heap allocation happens on the call path. The C box\nfunction still uses the same fixed signature\n(`int fn(const void **, const int *, int, void *, int, int *)`);\nthe JSON unwrap is transparent to it.\n\nThis slice unblocks issue 312's slice 4.5 — Lua now writes JSON\nfor cross-language outputs, and a Lua → C wire with a primitive\npayload (string or number) flows correctly end-to-end. The\npipeline integration test (`tests/maps/pipeline`) exercises this\npath: Lua doubles a number, C adds one, Bash exclaims, end-to-end.\n\n`tests/307-c-spec-test.c` gains three tests:\n`invoke_json_string_input` (quotes stripped),\n`invoke_json_number_input` (raw passthrough on JSON number),\n`invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json` (raw passthrough on parse\nfailure). `langs/c/Makefile` now folds in `libs/json/json.c`\nthe same way the Lua spec does."
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_018vjK8sxkJEBL1muMerqFHU"
      }]

          "replace_all":false,
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md",
          "old_string":"- **Slice 4.5 (2026-05-21) — per-wire writing style.** Each wire\n  keeps its own format. The dispatch picks the consumer slot's\n  native or JSON ring per outgoing connection based on\n  `output_edge_native[j]`, so a box with mixed fan-out (some\n  same-lang consumers, some cross-lang) lets each consumer get\n  the right format for its own wire. A per-call `output_native`\n  hint (true iff every outgoing wire is same-lang) is still passed\n  to the spec — specs that can pre-emptively pick a cheaper output\n  format when all consumers are same-lang may use it; current\n  specs ignore it. **The Lua spec still writes tostring bytes\n  regardless of the flag.** A full per-wire conversion (Lua writes\n  tostring, dispatch calls the spec's `native_to_json` bridge per\n  cross-language wire to get JSON bytes for those consumers)\n  requires the Lua spec's invoke to leave its return value on the\n  Lua stack so the bridge can read it — a contract change\n  deferred to a coordinated slice once the C and Bash specs grow\n  matching JSON-input handling (issues 307 / 308).",
          "new_string":"- **Slice 4.5 (2026-05-21) — per-wire writing style + Lua JSON\n  output.** Two coordinated halves:\n  - **Per-wire push.** Each wire keeps its own format. The\n    dispatch picks the consumer slot's native or JSON ring per\n    outgoing connection based on `output_edge_native[j]`. A box\n    with mixed fan-out (some same-lang consumers, some\n    cross-lang) lets each consumer get the right format for its\n    own wire.\n  - **Lua writes JSON when any consumer is cross-language.** The\n    spec passes `output_native = 1` to invoke if every outgoing\n    wire is same-language, else `0`. On the `0` branch the Lua\n    spec serializes the return via the same encoder that powers\n    the `native_to_json` bridge, so cross-language consumers\n    receive parseable JSON (numbers, strings, tables, arrays).\n    On `1` the spec keeps the existing tostring coercion. C-side\n    JSON-input acceptance landed in 307 alongside this, so a Lua\n    → C wire with a primitive payload now round-trips through\n    real JSON in both directions.     "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"All three tasks done. Plain English recap:\n\n**What changed under the hood.**\n\nTwo cooperating pieces of new behavior. The C side now knows that when a value arrives from a different language, the bytes might be JSON — so it gently unwraps the common cases (a JSON-quoted string gets its quotes peeled off; a JSON number passes through as-is; anything that doesn't parse as JSON gets passed through unchanged). The Lua side now knows when its return value is going to a different-language consumer and, in that case, serializes through the proper JSON encoder instead of the cheap-and-cheerful `tostring`. Same-language Lua-to-Lua wires still use the fast `tostring` path; nothing changed on the fast path.\n\n**What this unlocks.**\n\nA Lua-to-C wire now actually carries JSON across the boundary, in both directions:\n\n- Lua returns the number `10` → the wire carries `10` (the JSON encoding) → C unwraps it (no-op, already in the right form) → the C function reads `10` like a number.\n- Lua returns the string `\"hi\"` → the wire carries `\"hi\"` (JSON-quoted) → C unwraps the quotes → the C function reads `hi`.\n- Lua returns `{a=1, b=2}` → the wire carries `{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}` (proper JSON) → C currently passes it through as raw JSON bytes. Making C transparently project that into a typed C struct is the next deferred slice (typed-wrapper generation; tracked in issue 307 items 2–4).\n\nThe existing pipeline fixture (`Lua double → C addone → Bash shout`) now actually exercises this end-to-end — Lua emits real JSON numbers, C reads them, the chain works. The fixture's Lua function got a small tweak: it returns a number now instead of an explicitly-stringified number, because the wire encoder does that job better than user code does.\n\n**One known awkward case.**\n\nA box that sends its output to both a same-language and a different-language consumer at once writes JSON for both (because the producer writes once, and JSON is the safe choice). The same-language consumer ends up reading JSON bytes through what looks like its native compartment — Lua's input-side parse-with-fallback handles this fine for primitives, but it's not perfectly elegant. The deeper fix (producer leaves the value in its runtime; the dispatch converts per consumer) is captured in 312's status as a future slice.\n\n**Test results.**\n\nFull suite green. 22 slot-store + 14 graph-loader + 5 spec-registry + 7 dispatch + 3 jsonl + 4 event-queue + 8 large-value + 13 unified-allocator + 11 pool + 2 pool-spec-init + **9 Lua spec** (3 new for JSON input + 1 for merged-module) + **8 C spec (3 new for JSON input acceptance)** + 5 Bash spec + 22 JSON + 5 Lua-bridge + 11 integration tests including the multi-language `pipeline` map running through the real JSON wire.\n\n**Remaining task list across the issues:**\n\n- `issue 307` — items 2 (JSON output writing for C — needs typed wrappers), 3 (compile callback signature gains box pointer), 4 (per-box cflags/link_libs/headers).\n- `issue 312` — the awkward mixed-fan-out case noted above; only deeper contract changes will fix it.\n- `issue 318` — sentinel primitives implementation (`$ref`, `$function_pointer`, `$lang_opaque`).\n- `issue 308` — Bash side equivalents; Bash native form is strings so mostly cosmetic.\n- `issue 313` — C-side source merge and Bash-side script-sourcing; the inline-into-dispatch optimization.\n\nReady to either pick another task off the list or move to 313's next slice — your call."
      }]
  },

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.h",
    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,    /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,    /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,   /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics;     "originalFile":"/* langs/lang-spec.h — public interface for SoraMech language specs.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C contract that every language\n * spec (Lua, C, Bash, anything user-added) implements. The dispatch\n * layer prints the error context and aborts. There is no recovery,\n * no retry, no per-task failed state. This is intentional.\n *\n * Issue 312 extends this contract with optional fast-path\n * callbacks: `invoke_native` and `invoke_json` are specialised\n * variants the dispatch layer prefers when wire classification\n * says they apply; `native_to_json` and `json_to_native` are\n * bridges used at language boundaries. The spec\n * dispatches internally — its decoder for that input picks the\n * native or JSON path based on the flag.\n *\n * Per-output format flag (`output_native`): non-zero iff the\n * dispatch wants the spec to write native bytes to `out_buf`,\n * zero iff it wants JSON. The spec produces one form per call;\n * cross-language fan-out is handled by the dispatch layer, which\n * converts via `native_to_json` once and pushes the JSON to every\n * cross-language consumer.\n *\n * On non-dual-ring slots (single-language inputs or single-language\n * outputs only), the dispatch passes NULL for `input_native` and\n * 0 for `output_native`; the spec falls back to its default\n * decode (typically JSON, which Lua's existing bridge handles).\n * `input_native` may be NULL even when `n_inputs > 0` — specs\n * must check before dereferencing. */\ntypedef int (*lang_invoke_fn)(void *handle,\n                              const char *file_path,\n                              const char *fn_name,\n                              const void **input_data,\n                              const int   *input_sizes,\n                              const int   *input_native,\n                              int          n_inputs,\n                              int          output_native,\n                              void        *out_buf,\n                              int          out_buf_capacity,\n                              int         *out_size);\n\n/* Wire-format bridge: convert one direction of native ↔ JSON.\n * Used when a value crosses a language boundary. Spec sets one\n * or both; if NULL, the dispatch layer treats native and JSON as\n * identical byte streams (the current uniform-byte default).\n *\n * `handle` is the worker's per-language handle (the same one\n * `invoke` receives) — bridges may need it to reach a runtime-side\n * scratch area: Lua reads/writes via the lua_State stack, C may\n * keep a typed-pointer table, Bash may need its sub-process. For `json_to_native`:\n * the bridge pushes the reconstructed value onto the same store.\n * `src` / `dst` carry only the JSON side. */\ntypedef int (*lang_bridge_fn)(void *handle,\n                              const void *src, int src_size,\n                              void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lang_spec_t */\ntypedef struct lang_spec {\n    const char *name;       /* \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ... */\n    const char *file_ext;   /* \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"        */\n\n    /* init: once per worker thread at pool startup. Bytes on the wire are this language's\n     * native serialisation (Lua tables via msgpack, C struct\n     * memcpy, etc.) and the encode/decode round trip is skipped.\n     * NULL means the spec hasn't specialised; dispatch falls\n     * back to `invoke`. Issue 312. */\n    lang_invoke_fn invoke_native;\n\n    /* invoke_json — optional universal-interop path. Bytes on the\n     * wire are JSON. NULL means the spec hasn't specialised;\n     * dispatch falls back to `invoke`. Issue 312. */\n    lang_invoke_fn invoke_json;\n\n    /* Bridges between native and JSON wire forms. Normalised at runtime.       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\n/* Tagged so the forward declaration `typedef struct box box_t;` in\n * langs/lang-spec.h matches and the compile callback can accept a\n * `const box_t *` parameter. */\ntypedef struct box {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language.           "old_string":"/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) return -1;\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. */\n        execlp(\"gcc\", \"gcc\",\n               \"-shared\", \"-fPIC\", \"-O2\", \"-Wall\",\n               \"-o\", out_path, src_path, (char *)NULL);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    if (waitpid(pid, &status, 0) < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ split_cflags() — split a cflags string on whitespace\n *\n * gcc wants each token as a separate argv entry. The user's cflags\n * is a single string like \"-O0 -g -mavx2\" — we split it in place\n * (modifying `buf`) and stash the token pointers into `tokens`.\n * Returns the number of tokens; -1 on overflow. Tokens point into\n * `buf` and are valid for as long as `buf` is. */\nstatic int split_cflags(char *buf, char **tokens, int max_tokens)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    char *p = buf;\n    while (*p) {\n        while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\\t') p++;\n        if (!*p) break;\n        if (n >= max_tokens) return -1;\n        tokens[n++] = p;\n        while (*p && *p != ' ' && *p != '\\t') p++;\n        if (*p) *p++ = '\\0';\n    }\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC, plus per-box hints from box JSON\n *\n * When `box` is non-NULL the box's cflags / link_libs hints are\n * appended to the gcc command. Issue 307 items 3+4. When `box` is\n * NULL the call is the \"no box context\" path (e.g. the internal\n * lazy-compile when the dispatch hands the spec a raw `.c` ref) —\n * the default flags are still applied, no extras. */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path,\n                     const box_t *box)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n\n    /* Bounded argv: 16 fixed slots for \"-shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall\n     * -o out src\" plus headroom, 32 for cflags tokens, 32 for\n     * link-lib `-l` pairs. Anything larger is unusual and the\n     * caller can break up the work into multiple boxes. */\n    enum { ARGV_CAP = 96, CFLAG_TOK_CAP = 32 };\n    const char *argv_view[ARGV_CAP];\n    int n = 0;\n    argv_view[n++] = \"gcc\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-shared\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-fPIC\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-O2\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-Wall\";\n\n    /* Per-box cflags: split on whitespace into individual tokens. */\n    char  cflags_buf[1024];\n    char *cflag_tokens[CFLAG_TOK_CAP];\n    int   n_cflag_tokens = 0;\n    if (box && box->cflags && box->cflags[0]) {\n        size_t len = strlen(box->cflags);\n        if (len >= sizeof cflags_buf) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: cflags too long for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        memcpy(cflags_buf, box->cflags, len + 1);\n        n_cflag_tokens = split_cflags(cflags_buf, cflag_tokens, CFLAG_TOK_CAP);\n        if (n_cflag_tokens < 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: too many cflag tokens for box '%s'\\n\",\n                    box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_cflag_tokens; i++) {\n            if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: argv overflow for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            argv_view[n++] = cflag_tokens[i];\n        }\n    }\n\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-o\";\n    argv_view[n++] = out_path;\n    argv_view[n++] = src_path;\n\n    /* Per-box link libs: each becomes a `-l<name>` argv entry. The\n     * combined \"-l\" + name lives in a small per-lib heap allocation\n     * — n_link_libs is small so the cost is negligible. */\n    char *lflag_buf[ARGV_CAP];\n    int   n_lflags = 0;\n    if (box && box->link_libs && box->n_link_libs > 0) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < box->n_link_libs; i++) {\n            const char *libname = box->link_libs[i];\n            if (!libname || !*libname) continue;\n            size_t buflen = strlen(libname) + 3;   /* \"-l\" + name + NUL */\n            char *s = malloc(buflen);\n            if (!s) {\n                for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: oom assembling link_libs for '%s'\\n\",\n                        box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            snprintf(s, buflen, \"-l%s\", libname);\n            if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n                for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n                free(s);\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: argv overflow for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            lflag_buf[n_lflags++] = s;\n            argv_view[n++] = s;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n        for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    argv_view[n] = NULL;\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. execvp wants\n         * (char *const *), and we built (const char *) entries —\n         * the cast is safe because execvp doesn't modify them. */\n        execvp(\"gcc\", (char *const *)(void *)argv_view);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    int wait_rc = waitpid(pid, &status, 0);\n    for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n    if (wait_rc < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */"

The user's cflags\n * is a single string like \"-O0 -g -mavx2\" — we split it in place\n * (modifying `buf`) and stash the token pointers into `tokens`.\n * Returns the number of tokens; -1 on overflow. Tokens point into\n * `buf` and are valid for as long as `buf` is. */\nstatic int split_cflags(char *buf, char **tokens, int max_tokens)\n{\n    int n = 0;\n    char *p = buf;\n    while (*p) {\n        while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\\t') p++;\n        if (!*p) break;\n        if (n >= max_tokens) return -1;\n        tokens[n++] = p;\n        while (*p && *p != ' ' && *p != '\\t') p++;\n        if (*p) *p++ = '\\0';\n    }\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ c_compile() — gcc -shared -fPIC, plus per-box hints from box JSON\n *\n * When `box` is non-NULL the box's cflags / link_libs hints are\n * appended to the gcc command. Issue 307 items 3+4. When `box` is\n * NULL the call is the \"no box context\" path (e.g. the internal\n * lazy-compile when the dispatch hands the spec a raw `.c` ref) —\n * the default flags are still applied, no extras. */\nstatic int c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path,\n                     const box_t *box)\n{\n    if (!src_path || !out_path) return -1;\n\n    /* Bounded argv: 16 fixed slots for \"-shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall\n     * -o out src\" plus headroom, 32 for cflags tokens, 32 for\n     * link-lib `-l` pairs. Anything larger is unusual and the\n     * caller can break up the work into multiple boxes. */\n    enum { ARGV_CAP = 96, CFLAG_TOK_CAP = 32 };\n    const char *argv_view[ARGV_CAP];\n    int n = 0;\n    argv_view[n++] = \"gcc\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-shared\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-fPIC\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-O2\";\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-Wall\";\n\n    /* Per-box cflags: split on whitespace into individual tokens. */\n    char  cflags_buf[1024];\n    char *cflag_tokens[CFLAG_TOK_CAP];\n    int   n_cflag_tokens = 0;\n    if (box && box->cflags && box->cflags[0]) {\n        size_t len = strlen(box->cflags);\n        if (len >= sizeof cflags_buf) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: cflags too long for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        memcpy(cflags_buf, box->cflags, len + 1);\n        n_cflag_tokens = split_cflags(cflags_buf, cflag_tokens, CFLAG_TOK_CAP);\n        if (n_cflag_tokens < 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: too many cflag tokens for box '%s'\\n\",\n                    box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_cflag_tokens; i++) {\n            if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: argv overflow for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            argv_view[n++] = cflag_tokens[i];\n        }\n    }\n\n    argv_view[n++] = \"-o\";\n    argv_view[n++] = out_path;\n    argv_view[n++] = src_path;\n\n    /* Per-box link libs: each becomes a `-l<name>` argv entry. The\n     * combined \"-l\" + name lives in a small per-lib heap allocation\n     * — n_link_libs is small so the cost is negligible. */\n    char *lflag_buf[ARGV_CAP];\n    int   n_lflags = 0;\n    if (box && box->link_libs && box->n_link_libs > 0) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < box->n_link_libs; i++) {\n            const char *libname = box->link_libs[i];\n            if (!libname || !*libname) continue;\n            size_t buflen = strlen(libname) + 3;   /* \"-l\" + name + NUL */\n            char *s = malloc(buflen);\n            if (!s) {\n                for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: oom assembling link_libs for '%s'\\n\",\n                        box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            snprintf(s, buflen, \"-l%s\", libname);\n            if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n                for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n                free(s);\n                fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: argv overflow for box '%s'\\n\", box->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            lflag_buf[n_lflags++] = s;\n            argv_view[n++] = s;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (n >= ARGV_CAP) {\n        for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    argv_view[n] = NULL;\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        /* Child: replace ourselves with gcc. execvp wants\n         * (char *const *), and we built (const char *) entries —\n         * the cast is safe because execvp doesn't modify them. */\n        execvp(\"gcc\", (char *const *)(void *)argv_view);\n        _exit(127);\n    }\n    int status = 0;\n    int wait_rc = waitpid(pid, &status, 0);\n    for (int j = 0; j < n_lflags; j++) free(lflag_buf[j]);\n    if (wait_rc < 0) return -1;\n    if (!WIFEXITED(status) || WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"c spec: gcc failed for '%s' → '%s' (status=%d)\\n\",\n                src_path, out_path, status);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */",

(void)sizes; (void)n;\\n\"\n        \"    double v = sqrt(16.0);\\n\"\n        \"    int len = snprintf((char *)out_buf, (size_t)out_capacity,\\n\"\n        \"                       \\\"%g\\\", v);\\n\"\n        \"    *out_size = len; return 0;\\n\"\n        \"}\\n\",\n        fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    box_t hint;\n    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);\n    hint.id          = \"rootify\";\n    const char *libs[1] = { \"m\" };\n    hint.link_libs   = libs;\n    hint.n_link_libs = 1;\n\n    ASSERT(c->compile(src_path, so_path, &hint) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n    ASSERT(h);\n    char buf[16];           "old_string":"`tests/307-c-spec-test.c` gains three tests:\n`invoke_json_string_input` (quotes stripped),\n`invoke_json_number_input` (raw passthrough on JSON number),\n`invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json` (raw passthrough on parse\nfailure). `langs/c/Makefile` now folds in `libs/json/json.c`\nthe same way the Lua spec does.",
          "new_string":"`tests/307-c-spec-test.c` gains three tests:\n`invoke_json_string_input` (quotes stripped),\n`invoke_json_number_input` (raw passthrough on JSON number),\n`invoke_json_falls_back_on_non_json` (raw passthrough on parse\nfailure). `langs/c/Makefile` now folds in `libs/json/json.c`\nthe same way the Lua spec does.\n\n### compile callback signature + per-box build hints — 2026-05-21\n\nThe spec interface's `compile` callback grew a third parameter,\n`const box_t *box`. Calls with a real box record (compile-button\npipeline, future typed-wrapper generation) get access to the\nbox's identity and compile hints; the internal lazy-compile path\nin `maybe_lazy_compile` passes `NULL` because it operates on a\nraw `.c` ref with no box context. `langs/lang-spec.h` carries a\nforward `typedef struct box box_t;` so specs that don't read the\nfields don't need the loader header pulled in.\n\n`box_t` (in `src/010-graph-loader.h`) grew four optional fields,\nall parsed from the box JSON when present:\n\n- `cflags` — a single string of additional flags appended to gcc.\n  Whitespace-split into argv tokens at compile time.\n- `link_libs[]` — array of library names. Each becomes a\n  `-l<name>` argv entry. The pointer array is malloc'd and freed\n  by `graph_destroy`; the strings inside live in the JSON arena.\n- `headers[]` — array of header names. Parsed and stored; not yet\n  consumed by the spec. Lights up with wrapper generation.\n- `n_link_libs` / `n_headers` — counts.\n\n`langs/c/spec.c`'s `c_compile` walks the box's `cflags` and\n`link_libs` into a bounded argv (96 slots), forks gcc, and waits.\nThe previous fixed-flags-only execlp call is replaced by execvp\nso the variable arg list can flow through. Failure modes (cflags\ntoo long, too many tokens, argv overflow, oom) all return -1\nwith a stderr line naming the box id.\n\nTwo new end-to-end tests in `tests/307-c-spec-test.c`:\n\n- `compile_with_cflags` — a probe source whose return depends on\n  `#ifdef SORAMECH_FLAG_ON`. Builds twice: once with no hints\n  (returns \"off\"), once with `cflags=\"-DSORAMECH_FLAG_ON\"`\n  (returns \"on\"). Proves the cflags string reaches gcc.\n- `compile_with_link_libs` — a source that calls `sqrt(16.0)`\n  from `<math.h>`. Builds with `link_libs=[\"m\"]`, invokes,\n  receives \"4\". Proves the `-l<name>` translation works.\n\nThe compile pipeline (`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`) currently\nignores the box's cflags / link_libs when its informational\npre-compile of C boxes runs — the runtime lazy-compile is the\nauthoritative path. Cleaning that up so the pre-compile uses the\nsame flags is a small follow-on; out of scope for this slice."
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01EAGoT8MsL48Sywg7XJc1mD"
      }]

    },
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Plain-English recap:\n\n**What changed:**\n\nEach C box can now declare in its JSON which extra compiler flags it wants and which libraries to link against. Three new optional fields:\n\n- `cflags`: extra flags passed straight to the compiler. Useful for `-DSOMETHING`, `-O0 -g`, `-mavx2`, anything the user normally hands to `gcc`.\n- `link_libs`: an array of library names. Each becomes a `-lname` flag automatically. So `[\"m\", \"curl\"]` links the math library and libcurl.\n- `headers`: an array of header names. Parsed but not yet used — these light up when the C spec grows its typed-wrapper generation (the deferred item that lets a Lua box hand a table to a C box and have it arrive as a typed struct).\n\nThe spec interface itself grew a third parameter on its compile callback so the C spec can actually see the box record (and read those new fields). Lua and Bash specs don't have a compile callback so they're unaffected. The internal \"raw .c file passed at invoke time\" path passes `NULL` for the box — it doesn't have a box record to point at, just a file path.\n\n**Two new tests prove it works end-to-end:**\n\n- A small C source whose behavior depends on `#ifdef SORAMECH_FLAG_ON` — built once without the flag (returns \"off\"), once with `cflags=\"-DSORAMECH_FLAG_ON\"` (returns \"on\"). Proves the flag string reaches the compiler.\n- A C source that calls `sqrt(16.0)` from the math library — built with `link_libs=[\"m\"]` (`-lm`), invoked, returns \"4\". Proves the `-l<name>` translation works through the gcc invocation.\n\n**Test suite:** all green. 22 + 14 + 5 + 7 + 3 + 4 + 8 + 13 + 11 + 2 + 9 + **10** (C-spec, up from 8) + 5 + 22 + 5 + 11 = passing.\n\n**Remaining task list across the issues:**\n\n- `issue 307` item 2 — JSON output writing from C (needs typed wrappers); the `headers` field also goes live then.\n- `issue 312` — the mixed-fan-out same-language consumer awkward case (only a deeper contract change fixes it).\n- `issue 318` — sentinel primitives implementation.\n- `issue 308` — Bash side equivalents (small, mostly cosmetic).\n- `issue 313` — C-side concatenation, Bash sourcing, dispatch inlining.\n\nPicking the next one — the sentinel primitives (`issue 318`) feel like the highest-impact next step, since they're what unblock function pointers and shared-memory handles across language boundaries. Or 313's C-side concatenation if you'd rather keep the merge work going. Pick?"
      }]
  },

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Switching modes — let me walk through the design choices before diving in.\n\n**The thing that's been blocking 307 item 2:**\n\nThe C spec's invoke doesn't currently know what shape the user said the box returns. The box JSON declares `returns: \"int\"` or `returns: \"string\"` etc., but that information lives on the box record in the graph loader. The dispatch knows it, the spec doesn't.\n\nFor the C spec to write _real_ JSON on cross-language outputs (the symmetric of what Lua already does), it needs to look at that declared return type and pick the JSON shape: a `returns: \"string\"` should produce `\"hello\"` (with quotes and escaping), a `returns: \"int\"` should produce `42` (raw digits, which is valid JSON), and so on.\n\n**There are two ways to give the spec that information:**\n\n1. **Extend the invoke signature with `const box_t *box`** — symmetric with what we just did to compile, gives the spec full access to the box record, future-proof for things like sentinel primitives that need more box context.\n2. **Add a single `output_type` string parameter to invoke** — narrower, less invasive, but if we ever need anything else from the box record we're back here.\n\nOption 1 is the same flavor of cross-cutting change we did to compile, and it composes — once invoke has `box_t *`, sentinel primitives in 318 can use box->returns to decide which sentinel kind to emit, the typed-wrapper generation eventually uses it for input projection too. Option 2 closes a door we keep needing to reopen.\n\nI'm going to go with option 1. Here's the question I want you to think about while I do the mechanical part:\n\n**Question for the duck:** the C spec's \"wrap the bytes as JSON per declared type\" needs to handle `returns: \"string\"` specially (wrap + escape). For the other primitive types (`int`, `double`, `bool`), the C function's raw output is _already_ valid JSON — `42` is a JSON number, `true` is a JSON bool. So the C spec only really has work to do for strings and (future) tables. Does that match how you've been thinking about it? Or did you want stricter validation — make the C spec _check_ that the bytes match the declared type before passing them through?\n\nI'll start the work. Coming back to your answer."
      }]
  },

        "type":"text",
        "text":"**Concept check before moving on.** Now that the spec sees the box record at invoke time, it can read whatever fields the graph loader populated. The next step is making sure the `returns` field actually exists in `box_t` (right now boxes have `inputs` but no symmetric `returns`). \n\nA tiny design note worth pausing on: a box's `inputs` is an array of port declarations (because a box can have many input ports), but `returns` is a single value (because every box has exactly one output wire — that's the project's \"single output wire\" rule from issue 218). So we don't need an array — just one string for the declared return type."
      }]
  },

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.h",
    "originalFile":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,    /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,    /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,   /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\n/* Tagged so the forward declaration `typedef struct box box_t;` in\n * langs/lang-spec.h matches and the compile callback can accept a\n * `const box_t *` parameter. */\ntypedef struct box {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Per-box compile hints, optional, currently used by the C spec\n     * (issue 307). Lua / Bash boxes leave these at NULL / 0. All\n     * point into the graph's arena; no separate ownership. */\n    const char    *cflags;        /* extra flags appended to `cc`   */\n    int            n_link_libs;\n    const char   **link_libs;     /* each becomes `-l<name>`        */\n    int            n_headers;\n    const char   **headers;       /* `#include`d by generated wrappers */\n\n    /* Read boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (read only; ignored if value set) */\n    const char    *value;         /* inline literal; if set, read emits this directly */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language. When set, the dispatch\n     * passes the slot's bytes to invoke_native as-is; when cleared\n     * the dispatch calls json_to_native first.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, push native bytes\n     * directly; when cleared, call native_to_json first and push\n     * JSON. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). The pool's spec init can use this\n * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\nint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime attach (phase 5 + 7)\n *\n * Allocates one slot per input port for every box and resolves each\n * call box's language spec from the registry. After this call, the\n * dispatch layer can read inputs via `box->input_slot_ids[i]` and\n * invoke the spec via `spec_registry_at(r, box->spec_idx)`.\n *\n * Slot defaults for this iteration:\n *   - cell_capacity = `default_cell_bytes` (or 4096 if 0)\n *   - n_cells = 1 (peek mode)\n *   - flags = 0\n *\n * Iterator-fed wires and the multi-cell pop mode land in a follow-on\n * — they need compile-time wire classification (issue 305 phase 5\n * proper) that this iteration ducks. Returns 0 on success, -1 with\n * *err set on the first resolution or allocation failure. */\nstruct slot_store;        /* opaque forward decl */\nstruct spec_registry;     /* opaque forward decl */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store    *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int                   default_cell_bytes,\n                         char                **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "replaceAll":false,
    "structuredPatch":[{

      }],
    "newString":"    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    const char    *returns;       /* declared output type: \"string\"/\"int\"/\n                                   * \"double\"/\"bool\"/\"bytes\"/\"json\"/\"void\"\n                                   * or NULL when the user hasn't said.\n                                   * Read by specs on the JSON-output\n                                   * path (issue 307 item 2). */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */",

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"**Now the C spec's JSON-output branch.** Conceptually, the spec writes its bytes _twice_-conditionally:\n\n- `output_native = 1` → write the user function's raw bytes (existing behavior; the same-language fast path).\n- `output_native = 0` → wrap based on `box->returns`:\n  - `\"string\"` → JSON-quoted with escape sequences for `\"`, `\\`, control characters.\n  - `\"int\"` / `\"double\"` / `\"bool\"` / `\"null\"` / `\"json\"` → raw passthrough (already valid JSON).\n  - `\"void\"` → empty.\n  - missing / unknown → raw passthrough (safest fallback).\n\nJSON string escaping is straightforward but easy to get wrong. The `libs/json` library has a writer that handles escaping — `json_writer_string` writes a properly-escaped JSON string. I'll use it instead of hand-rolling."
      }]
  },

          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_invoke_string_output_jsonifies() — issue 307 item 2\n *\n * When the box declares `returns: \"string\"` and the dispatch asks\n * for JSON output (output_native=0), the spec wraps the user\n * function's raw bytes as a JSON string — quotes added, special\n * characters escaped. The echo function returns its input as a\n * raw string; we send it back as \"hi\" and verify the wire form\n * is the JSON-quoted \"\\\"hi\\\"\". */\nstatic int test_invoke_string_output_jsonifies(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    box_t hint;\n    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);\n    hint.id      = \"echo\";\n    hint.returns = \"string\";\n\n    const char *msg = \"hi\";\n    const void *args[1]  = { msg };\n    int         sizes[1] = { 2 };\n    char buf[64];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, NULL, 1, /*output_native=*/0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 4);                /* \"\\\"hi\\\"\" — four bytes */\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"\\\"hi\\\"\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_string_output_native_passthrough() — issue 307 item 2\n *\n * When the dispatch asks for native (output_native=1), the spec\n * leaves the user's bytes alone regardless of the declared return\n * type. Same-language fast path keeps strings raw. */\nstatic int test_invoke_string_output_native_passthrough(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n    char so_path[256];\n    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    box_t hint;\n    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);\n    hint.id      = \"echo\";\n    hint.returns = \"string\";\n\n    const char *msg = \"hi\";\n    const void *args[1]  = { msg };\n    int         sizes[1] = { 2 };\n    char buf[64];\n    int n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"echo\",\n                       args, sizes, NULL, 1, /*output_native=*/1,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 2);                /* \"hi\" — raw bytes */\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hi\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_invoke_int_output_passthrough() — issue 307 item 2\n *\n * Declared `returns: \"int\"`. The function writes \"42\" — already a\n * valid JSON number — and the JSON output mode passes those bytes\n * through unchanged. */\nstatic int test_invoke_int_output_passthrough(void)\n{\n    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;\n    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);\n    ASSERT(c);\n\n    char src_path[256], so_path[256];\n    snprintf(src_path, sizeof src_path,\n             \"/tmp/soramech-int-%d.c\", (int)getpid());\n    snprintf(so_path,  sizeof so_path,\n             \"/tmp/soramech-int-%d.so\", (int)getpid());\n    FILE *fp = fopen(src_path, \"w\");\n    ASSERT(fp);\n    fputs(\n        \"#include <stdio.h>\\n\"\n        \"int forty_two(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\\n\"\n        \"              void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size) {\\n\"\n        \"    (void)inputs; (void)sizes; (void)n;\\n\"\n        \"    int written = snprintf((char *)out_buf, (size_t)out_capacity, \\\"%d\\\", 42);\\n\"\n        \"    *out_size = written; return 0;\\n\"\n        \"}\\n\",\n        fp);\n    fclose(fp);\n\n    ASSERT(c->compile(src_path, so_path, NULL) == 0);\n    void *h = c->init(0);\n\n    box_t hint;\n    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);\n    hint.id      = \"forty_two\";\n    hint.returns = \"int\";\n\n    char buf[16];\n    int  n = 0;\n    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"forty_two\",\n                       NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, /*output_native=*/0,\n                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);\n    ASSERT(rc == 0);\n    ASSERT(n == 2);\n    buf[n] = '\\0';\n    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);\n\n    c->teardown(h);\n    unlink(so_path);\n    unlink(src_path);\n    spec_registry_destroy(r);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    if (stat(\"langs/c/spec.so\", &st) != 0 ||\n        stat(\"tests/maps/hello/src/echo.c\", &st) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"307-c-spec-test: spec or fixture not built;         "lines":[" }"," /* }}} */"," ","+/* {{{ test_invoke_string_output_jsonifies() — issue 307 item 2","+ *","+ * When the box declares `returns: \"string\"` and the dispatch asks","+ * for JSON output (output_native=0), the spec wraps the user","+ * function's raw bytes as a JSON string — quotes added, special","+ * characters escaped. */","+static int test_invoke_string_output_jsonifies(void)","+{","+    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;","+    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);","+    ASSERT(c);","+    char so_path[256];","+    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);","+    void *h = c->init(0);","+","+    box_t hint;","+    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);","+    hint.id      = \"echo\";","+    hint.returns = \"string\";","+","+    const char *msg = \"hi\";","+    const void *args[1]  = { msg };","+    int         sizes[1] = { 2 };","+    char buf[64];","+    int n = 0;","+    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"echo\",","+                       args, sizes, NULL, 1, /*output_native=*/0,","+                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);","+    ASSERT(rc == 0);","+    ASSERT(n == 4);                /* \"\\\"hi\\\"\" — four bytes */","+    buf[n] = '\\0';","+    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"\\\"hi\\\"\") == 0);","+","+    c->teardown(h);","+    unlink(so_path);","+    spec_registry_destroy(r);","+    return 1;","+}","+/* }}} */","+","+/* {{{ test_invoke_string_output_native_passthrough() — issue 307 item 2","+ *","+ * When the dispatch asks for native (output_native=1), the spec","+ * leaves the user's bytes alone regardless of the declared return","+ * type. Same-language fast path keeps strings raw. */","+static int test_invoke_string_output_native_passthrough(void)","+{","+    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;","+    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);","+    ASSERT(c);","+    char so_path[256];","+    ASSERT(compile_echo(c, so_path, sizeof so_path) == 0);","+    void *h = c->init(0);","+","+    box_t hint;","+    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);","+    hint.id      = \"echo\";","+    hint.returns = \"string\";","+","+    const char *msg = \"hi\";","+    const void *args[1]  = { msg };","+    int         sizes[1] = { 2 };","+    char buf[64];","+    int n = 0;","+    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"echo\",","+                       args, sizes, NULL, 1, /*output_native=*/1,","+                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);","+    ASSERT(rc == 0);","+    ASSERT(n == 2);","+    buf[n] = '\\0';","+    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"hi\") == 0);","+","+    c->teardown(h);","+    unlink(so_path);","+    spec_registry_destroy(r);","+    return 1;","+}","+/* }}} */","+","+/* {{{ test_invoke_int_output_passthrough() — issue 307 item 2","+ *","+ * Declared `returns: \"int\"`. The function writes \"42\" — already a","+ * valid JSON number — and the JSON output mode passes those bytes","+ * through unchanged. */","+static int test_invoke_int_output_passthrough(void)","+{","+    spec_registry_t *r = NULL;","+    const lang_spec_t *c = load_c_spec(&r);","+    ASSERT(c);","+","+    char src_path[256], so_path[256];","+    snprintf(src_path, sizeof src_path,","+             \"/tmp/soramech-int-%d.c\", (int)getpid());","+    snprintf(so_path,  sizeof so_path,","+             \"/tmp/soramech-int-%d.so\", (int)getpid());","+    FILE *fp = fopen(src_path, \"w\");","+    ASSERT(fp);","+    fputs(","+        \"#include <stdio.h>\\n\"","+        \"int forty_two(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\\n\"","+        \"              void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size) {\\n\"","+        \"    (void)inputs; (void)sizes; (void)n;\\n\"","+        \"    int written = snprintf((char *)out_buf, (size_t)out_capacity, \\\"%d\\\", 42);\\n\"","+        \"    *out_size = written; return 0;\\n\"","+        \"}\\n\",","+        fp);","+    fclose(fp);","+","+    ASSERT(c->compile(src_path, so_path, NULL) == 0);","+    void *h = c->init(0);","+","+    box_t hint;","+    memset(&hint, 0, sizeof hint);","+    hint.id      = \"forty_two\";","+    hint.returns = \"int\";","+","+    char buf[16];","+    int  n = 0;","+    int rc = c->invoke(h, &hint, so_path, \"forty_two\",","+                       NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, /*output_native=*/0,","+                       buf, sizeof buf, &n);","+    ASSERT(rc == 0);","+    ASSERT(n == 2);","+    buf[n] = '\\0';","+    ASSERT(strcmp(buf, \"42\") == 0);","+","+    c->teardown(h);","+    unlink(so_path);","+    unlink(src_path);","+    spec_registry_destroy(r);","+    return 1;","+}","+/* }}} */","+"," /* {{{ main() */"," int main(void)"," {"]
      },{
